issue.title: Build Prepare for Offline Screen Download Controls
issue.body: Once a translator initiates a download on the Prepare for Offline screen, the Download button is replaced by controls that let them manage the in-progress download. This ticket builds the Pause, Resume, and Cancel controls that appear after download begins, and the per-item progress indicator in the tier list. ## Functional Requirements ### Control States - Once the download begins, replace the Download button with Pause and Cancel controls. - When the translator taps Pause, suspend the active download and replace the Pause control with Resume; retain all progress made so far. - When the translator taps Resume, continue the download from where it was paused and restore the Pause control. - Display Pause (`li:pause`) and Cancel (`li:x`) as the active controls during download; display Resume (`li:play`) and Cancel during a paused state. - Tapping Cancel stops the download immediately and restores the Download button (see #51); no confirmation dialog is shown since progress is saved and the download resumes automatically on the next WiFi connection. ### Per-Item Progress Indicator - While an item is actively downloading, its selector circle transforms into a circular progress ring that fills as the download progresses, with a `li:download` arrow centered inside it animating in a slow vertical bounce. - When the item finishes downloading, its selector circle becomes a green filled circle (`li:circle-check`) and the progress ring moves to the next item in the download queue. - Items not yet reached in the download order remain in their pre-download selector state. --- ## Engineering context *(Added for implementation readiness. Product requirements above remain the source of truth.)* ### Product intent (summary) After download starts, replace the Download CTA with Pause / Resume / Cancel and show per-item progress in the resource list. ### Proposed technical approach 1. Share download **session state** with #51 (idle | downloading | paused | cancelled). 2. Map controls: downloading → Pause+Cancel; paused → Resume+Cancel; cancel → back to Download CTA (#51) while retaining partial files for Wi‑Fi resume. 3. Drive per-item circular progress from queue worker events; completed → checkmark; advance active item. 4. Resume-on-next-Wi‑Fi after Cancel is engine policy — implement in the shared download service (same module as #51 start), not only in UI. ### Systems / modules / anchors - UI: extend Prepare for Offline resources section from #51 - State: new hook e.g. `usePrepareOfflineDownload` reading queue/worker - Connectivity: `src/services/connectivity.ts` / NetInfo for Wi‑Fi resume - Persistence: same download_queue store as #51/#147 ### Implementation steps 1. Define session state machine + UI bindings. 2. Implement Pause (suspend worker), Resume (continue), Cancel (stop; keep partials; restore CTA). 3. Bind progress ring + bounce download icon to active item; checkmark on complete. 4. Ensure cancel does not clear #39 download-started if product still considers prep initiated — **see Open questions**. 5. Tests for control state transitions and progress rendering. ### Dependencies & prerequisites - **In-repo:** #51 (summary + Download start + shared engine). Related #39, #147 (queue progress on Sync), #53. - **External:** Same API/download URLs as #51. ### Edge cases & failure states - Pause across app kill: restore paused vs downloading on next launch. - Cancel then Wi‑Fi resume: must not surprise-upload; only resume **downloads**. - Item failure: retry policy TBD — do not block entire queue without UX (open question). - Rapid Pause/Resume tapping: debounce / disable while transitioning. ### Testing & verification - Unit: state machine transitions. - Component: control visibility per state; progress ring on active row. - Manual Android: pause retains bytes; resume continues; cancel restores Download button; leave app and return. ### Analytics / observability / migrations - Log pause/resume/cancel with session id; no file contents. ### Assumptions - “Progress is saved” means partial files + queue cursor are durable. - Per-item animation can be simplified if performance demands, but states must match product. ### Open questions 1. After Cancel, does #39 remain “download started” (no re-surface) or reset? 2. Failed item: skip, retry N times, or fail the session? 3. Should Cancel require Wi‑Fi to auto-resume later even if user is on cellular? ### Acceptance criteria - [ ] After download begins, Download CTA is replaced by Pause + Cancel. - [ ] Pause ↔ Resume swaps controls and retains progress. - [ ] Cancel stops download, restores Download CTA, keeps partial progress for later Wi‑Fi resume. - [ ] Active item shows progress ring + download icon; completed shows green check; untouched items stay pre-download. - [ ] Tests cover control states; Android manual QA for pause/resume/cancel.

comments.body:
## API readiness note (board audit — refreshed)

**Why the API is not complete for this ticket**

Pause/Resume/Cancel + per-item progress rings are mostly **mobile UI over the #201 queue**. Real progress still needs **downloadable URLs + sizes**. Since #295, many Tier 2/3 items resolve via **direct Aquifer**; fluent-api still does not provide a unified offline catalog, and **Tier 1 Source Audio (DBL) remains missing**.

### What exists today

- fluent-api `main` @ `28f9bdb`: bible text bulk endpoints; no resource-manifest / source-audio catalog.
- Mobile: download queue + worker (#295); Prepare Offline UI can drive pause/resume/cancel against queued Aquifer/Fluent-text items when `sourceUrl` is set.
- Documented gap: Source Audio expected from DBL — no Fluent/DBL contract yet.

### What is missing

1. fluent-api (or DBL-via-Fluent) **source audio** download URLs + byte sizes for Tier 1 progress accuracy.
2. Optional authoritative manifest from fluent-api so controls are not coupled to Aquifer response quirks / client API keys.
3. Clear failure policy for missing URLs (skip vs fail session) — shared with #201.

### What needs to be done

1. Ship DBL/Fluent source-audio assets for Tier 1 (blocks complete Prepare Offline audio downloads).
2. Confirm whether Aquifer-direct manifests are accepted long-term; if not, add fluent-api proxy/catalog.
3. Mobile #52: wire controls to queue session state; progress rings work for any queued item with `sourceUrl` — mock/fixture remaining gaps rather than inventing a permanent client-only contract.

Checked against fluent-api `main` @ `28f9bdb` (2026-08-06). Prior audit was `3ef4025` (2026-07-31).
